text: Six months after Theo Bryant's first Azure migration, Driftwood Outdoor Apparel has grown, and so has the mess. A dozen services now ship weekly, each one standing on its own infrastructure, none of it coordinated. Driftwood's new CTO, Dana Whitfield, orders a company-wide platform review alongside VP of Engineering Casey Lindqvist.

The review comes back with three blunt findings: no shared platform across teams, no credible cost or capacity forecast for ten times the normal traffic, and no shared visibility when something breaks. Those three gaps become the mandate — migrate services onto Kubernetes at real scale, across both clouds, with one shared FinOps dashboard.

It's tempting to point at the intermediate project as proof this already works. Dana's pushback is the thesis of this whole capstone: one app surviving one deploy on one node is a different claim from a dozen services, scaled under real holiday traffic, staying inside budget. The second claim has to be proven, not assumed from the first.

This lesson only covers why the ask grew into a mandate, and who's now accountable for it. Scope, cloud architecture, and what the dashboard actually measures are still open questions — Lesson 2 turns this mandate into an actual plan.
